 COMMON JUDGMENT  These two petitions are brought U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act 1988 for the compensation of Rs.30,00,000/
and Rs.10,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the petitioner and for the death of Sri.P.Venki Rao, in the road traffic accident caused on 27.12.2022.
 02.
Hence these two petitions were clubbed together for the purpose of recording common evidence.

The main petition is M.V.C.No.630/2023 and it is clubbed with M.V.C.No.2171/2023.
 03.
The brief facts in M.V.C.No.630/2023 are as under:

It is submitted that on 27.12.2022 at about 04.00 a.m., when the deceased namely P.Venki Rao was driving the goods carrier vehicle bearing No.
KA08A1346 from Rayachoty towards Madanapalle  (SCCH3) 4 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 along with cleaner namely P.Bhanuprasad, near Star Pipe Factory, MadanapalleRayachoty Road, one Bus Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
2 bearing No.KL06E7788 came with high speed, in rash and negligent manner came to wrong side and dashed against the goods vehicle.

entities.text: Bus Govindu P vs Subramanyam D
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As a result the driver of the goods vehicle caught in the seat and suffered severe injuries.
Then he was shifted to Government hospital, Rayachoty and after first aid he was referred to Sankalpa hospital, Tirupathi.
But inspite of best treatment he had succumbed to the injuries on same day at about 08.30 a.m.
Then the post mortem was conducted and handed over dead body to the petitioners.
Then the dead body was shifted to the native place and funeral ceremony took place by spending more than Rs.1,50,000/ towards treatment and other incidental charges.

That the deceased was hale and healthy prior to the accident and he was working as driver and earning Rs.25,000/
p.m.
Due to the death the petitioners have lost their only bread earner to the family.
The petitioners have lost their loving son and brother in the accident.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus driver.
Even an criminal case was registered the  (SCCH3) 5 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 said bus driver.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the bus.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
Hence this petition.
04. The brief facts in MVC.No.2171/2023 are as under:

It is submitted that on 27.12.2022 at about 04.00 a.m, when the petitioner was prooceeding as cleaner in the goods carrier vehicle bearing No.
KA08A1346 driven by one P.Venki Rao from Rayachoty towards Madanapalle, near Star Pipe Factory, MadanapalleRayachoty Road, one Bus bearing No.KL06E7788 came with high speed, in rash and negligent manner came to wrong side and dashed against the goods vehicle.
As a result the petitioner suffered severe injuries.

Then he was shifted to Government hospital, Rayachoty and after first aid he was shifted to Sankalpa hospital, Tirupathi,
wherein Xrays were taken and treated as inpatient.
The petitioner has spent huge amount of Rs.1,00,000/ towards treatment and other incidental charges.
The doctor has advised for future treatment and bed rest.

According to the petitioner he was hale  (SCCH3) 6 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 and healthy prior to accident and was working as Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
3 cleaner and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m.
Due to the injuries suffered, he is unable to attend to his work and daily routine activities and lost his income.
The accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus driver.
Even an criminal case was registered the said bus driver.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the bus.
Hence both respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
05. After service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared before this court and hence he was placed absent through out the proceedings of the petition.
However the respondent No.2 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement in both cases.
06. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.2 in both petitions are as under:
This respondent has denied the case of both petitioners.
This respondent has issued the policy in the name of one Smt.Siddappagari Syamala which is valid from 03.03.2022 to 02.03.2023.
But this respondent does not know who is the respondent No.1.
(SCCH3) 7 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23
The liability of the policy is subject to terms and conditions.
It is denied that this accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the bus driver, but due to the negligence of the deceased himself.
The bus driver and the deceased have no valid driving licence on the date of accident.
The bus is not involved in the alleged accident.

This respondent has denies the age,
avocation, income, loss of income and expenses details furnished by both petitioners.
The claim of the petitioners are exorbitant and excessive and prays to dismiss both petitions with costs.
07. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 and petitioner of both petitions were got examined themselves as PW.1 and 2 and got marked 13 documents as per Ex.P.1 to 13 and closed their side.
08. By way of rebuttal the respondent No.2 submit no oral evidence.

09. Heard both sides in both petitions.
 10.

Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed : 
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.630/2023  01.
Whether petitioners prove that they are  the LRs/dependants of deceased Sri.P.Venki  Rao S/o P.Govindu?

(SCCH3) 8 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
4

sentences.text:
02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased  Sri.P.Venki Rao S/o P.Govindu died in RTA  arising out of the accident alleged to have  been taken place on 27.12.2022 at about  04.00 a.m., on MadanapalleRaychoty Road,
 near Star Pipe Factory, due to negligent act of  driving of the Bus bearing registration No.
 KL06E7788 by its driver as alleged in the  petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for  compensation?

If so, what amount & from  whom?
 04. What order or award?
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.2171/2023  01.

Whether the petitioner prove that he has  sustained grievous injuries in the accident  occurred on 27.12.2022 at about 04.00 a.m.,
 near Star Pipe Factory, on Rayachoty  Madanapalle Road, Annamayya District,
 Andhra Pradesh., due to rash and negligent act  of driving of the bus bearing registration  No.KL06E7788 by its driver as alleged in the  petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for  compensation?

If, so, to what amount and  from whom?
 03.
What Order
or Award?

My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under:
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.630/2023  Issue No.1 : In affirmative  Issue No.2 : In affirmative  Issue No.3 : In partly affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order

for the following:
 ISSUES IN M.V.C.No.2171/2023
Issue No.1 : In affirmative

Issue No.2 : In affirmative Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
5
Issue No.3 :

As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  12. Issues No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.No.630/2023 and issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.2171/2023: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are inter related with each other and common in order to avoid repetition of facts.
 13.
According to the petitioners, the bus driver bearing No.KL06E7788 has caused the accident.

Thereby the son of the petitioner No.1 in  (SCCH3) 10 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 M.V.C.No.630/23 and the petitioner in M.V.C.
No.2171/23 have sustained injuries.
The same was opposed by the respondent No.2 and stated that this accident occurred due to the negligence of the goods driver only and hence they are not liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
14. To prove this the petitioner No.1 in M.V.C.No.630/23 was got examined himself as PW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.1 in his cross examination has admitted that "I have not seen the accident.
That one Bhanuprasad had informed me about the accident occurred by bus.
It is true that on the date of accident itself my son succumbed to injuries.
That I am doing agriculture work".
The PW.1 had denied all other suggestion of respondent No.2.
The PW.1 had not seen the accident but he had deposed based upon the records.
15. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2171/23 was got examined himself as PW.2 by reiterating all the averments of the petition in his affidavit.
The PW.2 in his cross examination has admitted that "The said goods vehicle was driven by one Venki Rao.
It is true  (SCCH3) 11 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 that the accident occurred on head on collusion.
That after the accident I was taken in 108 vehicle to Rayachoti hospital.
It is true that only first aid was given at Rayachoti hospital.
That I had obtained treatment as inpatient at Sankalpa hospital, Tirupathi for about 01 day.
It is true that I had not sustained fracture injuries".
The PW.2 has denied all the other suggestion of the respondent No.2 counsel.

16. The respondent No.2 contend that their bus Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
6 driver did not caused accident but it is due to the negligence of the driver of goods vehicle/deceased the accident occurred.
But in order to prove their contention they have not got examined any witness or not produced any documents.

In absence of any documents it is difficult to accept the contention of the respondent No.2.
 17.
The PW.1 and 2 have got marked the police documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 and 11.

So on perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation has filed chargesheet against the bus driver who had caused accident to the petitioner and to the son of petitioner No.1.

The said I.O has drawn spot mahazar and sketch which is well  (SCCH3) 12 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 corroborated with the contention of the petitioners that the cleaner and driver of the goods vehicle have sustained injuries due ot the accident caused accident by the bus driver.
The bus driver has not challenged the chargesheet filed against him.
There are no supportive documents on behalf of the respondent No.2 to show that their bus driver was not at fault.
Even there are no documents to show that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the goods vehicle driver/deceased.
18. In order to prove the dependency and legal heirs of deceased, the PW.1 has got marked the Aadhaar cards of the petitioners and deceased as per Ex.P.7 to 10.

So on perusal of these documents it is true that the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/23 are the parents and sister of the deceased and they have to be considered as legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.

Hence from the above documents and in absence of any other supportive documents on behalf of the respondents, I am of opinion that the bus driver had caused accident to the petitioner and to the son of petitioner No.1 and they have sustained injuries.

At this stage I would like to rely upon Judgment reported in  a) ILR 2016 KAR 55 - M/s ICICI Lombard GIC Ltd., V/s Smt.Bharthi S. Reddy and others - It is observed that the chargesheet filed by the jurisdictional police is the conclusive proof and that the same has not been questioned or challenged by the insurer.

sentences.text:
b) ILR 2003 KAR 409 - P.Varalakshmi Reddy Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
7 and others V/s The Karnataka State Road Transportation Corporation -

entities.text: P.Varalakshmi Reddy Govindu P vs Subramanyam D
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is observed that the tribunal on basis of evidence on record has to decide whether there is contributory negligence or not.
The tribunal has to find out the contributory negligence from the sketch drawn by the concerned police.
c) ILR 2009 KAR 385 - Smt.Nasreen Banu and others
V/s The Divisional Manager and another
- It is observed that the negligence of offending vehicle need not be established beyond reasonable doubt like that of penal action case.
One cannot loose sight of Evidence Act and in civil case it is purely based on facts.
(SCCH3) 14 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23  20. Therefore, in my opinion there is no material to discard the fact that the petitioners have suffered injuries in the accident caused by bus driver.

Hence,
in my opinion the petitioners are successful in proving these issues.
Hence I answered the issues No.1 and 2 in M.V.C.No.630/23 in affirmative and issue No.1 in M.V.C.No.2171/23 in affirmative.

21. Issue No.3 in M.V.C.630/23 and issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2171/23: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts.
 22.
Further the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/23 contended that deceased P.Venki Rao died in road traffic accident which took place on 27.12.2022 due to the rash and negligent manner driving of bus driver.
Further they have contended that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earner and facing financial problems and mental stress.
Hence, they have claimed compensation.

23 . Per contra, the same was denied by respondents No.2 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of bus driver but  (SCCH3) 15 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 due to negligence of deceased himself.
Hence the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.

24. The petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/23 being the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased are entitled for the compensation as under :
 a. Loss of dependency:-
The petitioners submitted that the deceased was aged about 19 years as on the date of accident.

To prove the same, the PW.1 has produced and got marked the Aadhaar card Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
8 of the deceased as per Ex.P.7 which reveals that the deceased was born on 28.12.2003.
So as on the date of accident the deceased would be 19 years and the same is considered for calculating the compensation.
So, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the multiplier applicable is "18" and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In order to prove the income of the deceased, the PW.1 had not produced any documents.
Under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider the notional income.
The date of accident was in the year 2022.

Under these circumstances it is just and proper to consider the Minimum Wages Act by considering the  (SCCH3) 16 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 deceased as semi skilled job as he was working as driver which comes to Rs.14,469/ per month.

Since the deceased has left three dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 2 to 3, then personal deduction is to be 1/3rd.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this case 1/3rd deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.

So, after deduction of 1/3rd (Rs.4,823/), then the income comes to Rs.9,646/.
 As above stated that apart from the deceased there are no one to look after the petitioners.
As per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the petitioners are entitled for future prospects.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The deceased being self employed and aged below 40 years,
then 40% (Rs.3,858/) to be added towards future prospects, the income for calculation comes to Rs.13,504/.
Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.13,504 x 12 x 18 = Rs.29,16,864/ under this head.
(SCCH3) 17 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23  b) Loss of estate and funeral expenses:

Since it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in AIR 2017 SC 5157 that the dependents would be entitled for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of Rs.15,000/, as such I award the same.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in AIR 2017 SC 5157
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: c) Loss of consortium:

In this case the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the parents of the Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
9 deceased are entitled for Rs.40,000/ each towards filial consortium. But the petitioner No.3 being the sister who is under care and custody of the petitioner No.1 is not entitled for any future prospects

as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur & Ors case and Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130. Hence I award the same.

25 . Thus the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/23 are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
 (SCCH3) 18 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 1.Loss of dependency Rs.29,16,864/
2.Loss of estate 15,000/
3.Towards filial consortium (for 80,000/
petitioners No.1 and 2 )
4.Transportation of dead body 15,000/
and funeral expenses
Further the petitioner in M.V.C.No.2171/2023 had contend that immediately after the accident he was taken to the hospital and admitted as inpatient.
He had incurred huge expenses towards hospitalisation, medical expenses etc,.
Due to the accident the petitioner had sustained disability and he had lost his income.
Hence he had filed this petition claiming compensation.
27. The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2171/2023 to prove the severity of the injuries and the treatment taken, has not got examined any doctor or other witnesses.
Even the petitioner has not produced any documents.
This petitioner has not produced any documents to show his income and lost of income due to the accident.
Even there are no documents to show that the petitioner required future medical treatment and expenses.
Hence this petitioner is not entitled for  (SCCH3) 19 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 any amount under the head of loss of future income and towards future medical expenses.

28. Considering the nature of injuries suffered and line of treatment obtained by PW.2 he is entitled for the compensation under the following heads :
Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
10  a. Pain and suffering during treatment period:
It is true that the PW.2 had not produced any Discharge summary to show that he was admitted in hospital as inpatient.
But the PW.2 might have spent some amount.
Hence I deem it fit to award Rs.20,000/ under this head.
b. Loss of amenities and nutrition food:
The PW.2 has stated that he has incurred huge expenses at the time of treatment.
In this regard he had not produced any supportive documents.
Hence in absence of this the PW.2 might had incurred some expenses.

Hence I deem it fit to award Rs.10,000/
under this head.
c. Towards attendent charges and conveyance: Further the PW.2 has not produced any documents to show that he was admitted as inpatient.
Hence under these circumstances I just feel it proper not to award any amount under this head.
(SCCH3) 20 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23  d.
Towards medical expenses:
The PW.2 has got marked the entire medical bills as per Ex.P.13 which amounts to Rs.11,276/.

Considering the bills,
I am of the opinion to award the said amount.
Hence the PW.2 is entitled for Rs.11,276/ under this head.
e. Towards loss of income during treatment period:
It is true that after the accident the PW.2 could not do any work for about 15 days and he is entitled for Rs.6,000/ under this head.

29 . Therefore, the petitioner of M.V.C.
No.2171/23 is entitled for total compensation of Rs.47,276/ (Forty seven thousand two hundred and seventy six only).
30 . Regarding liability:
As held on above issues the respondents failed to prove their defence.
The respondent No.2 eventhough in the written statement has stated that they have not issued the policy in the name of the respondent No.1.
But during the course of argument they have admitted this.
It is true that the respondent No.2 have issued policy in the name of the respondent No.1 which was in force as on the date of accident.
Hence the respondents No.1  (SCCH3) 21 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

31. With regard to apportionment of Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
11 compensation amount in M.V.C.No.630/2023 the petitioner No.1 and 2 being the parents are entitled for 40% each and the petitioner No.3 being the sister of the deceased is entitled for 20% of the total awarded amount.
Hence I answered the issue No.3 in M.V.C.No.630/2023 in partly affirmative and issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2171/2023 in partly affirmative.

32. Issue No.4 in M.V.C.630/2023 and issue No.3 in M.V.C.2171/2023: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration as they are inter related with each other and common in order to avoid repetition of facts.

33. In view of my findings on above Issues and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.

As such I proceed to pass the following:
 (SCCH3) 22 MVC.No.630/23 c/w  MVC.No.2171/23  ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/2023 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioners in M.V.C.No.630/2023 are entitled for Rs.30,26,864/ (Thirty lakhs twenty six thousand eight hundred and sixty four only) compensation with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
However in view of holding valid policy the respondent No.2 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
On deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for 40% each and the petitioner No.3 is entitled for 20% of the award amount.

Out of the share amount of the deposit of the compensation amount together with interest, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are entitled for release of 60% each of the amount shall be released to them through (SCCH3) 23 MVC.No.630/23 c/w MVC.No.2171/23 Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The remaining 40% each of the share amount shall be deposited in their names in any nationalized or schedule bank of their choice for a period of three years.

However, they are at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on the deposit amount from Govindu P vs Subramanyam D on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/55486825/
12 time to time.

Out of the share amount of petitioner No.3 along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized or schedule bank till she attain the age of majority, on proper identification.
However, the petitioner No.1 is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time and to use the same for the benefit of the minor petitioner No.3.
The claim petition filed by the petitioner in M.V.C.No.2171/2023 U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part, with costs.

The petitioner in M.V.C.No.2171/2023 is entitled for Rs.47,276/ (Forty seven thousand two hundred and seventy six only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
(SCCH3) 24 MVC.No.630/23 c/w MVC.No.2171/23 The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However in view of holding valid policy the respondent No.2 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act.
The entire compensation amount awarded to the petitioner along with interest accrued shall be released to him through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
The original Judgment shall be kept in M.V.C.No.630/2023 and copy of the same shall be kept in M.V.C.No.2171/2023.
The advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/ each.
Draw award accordingly.
